coverage.notes: SEL: NDE's Office for a Safe & Respectful Learning Environment publishes 'Nevada Social Emotional Learning Standards' (2-page PDF, 'Revised Standards with Definitions', file dated April 2025): 15 numbered standards grouped under the five CASEL competency names. The PDF has no grade bands and no per-grade benchmarks; NDE's pre-K standards page confirms 'K-12 NV SEL standards' exist and that SE standards were redeveloped in 2025. NDE's SEL page says Nevada adopted CASEL's five competencies as guidance in 2017 (per the 'SEL in Nevada' PDF). Portrait: NDE's Future of Learning Network page presents the 'Portrait of a Nevada Learner' (co-designed 2021-22) as the state's guiding vision, so pogStatus is statewide. Reviewer: I did not find a State Board adoption record for either document; confirm formal status with NDE.

frameworks.name: Nevada Social Emotional Learning Standards (Revised 2025)
frameworks.issuingBody: Nevada Department of Education, Office for a Safe & Respectful Learning Environment
frameworks.notes: Read from the NDE PDF https://webapp-strapi-paas-prod-nde-001.azurewebsites.net/uploads/sel_standards_with_definitions_d8b61da366.pdf (linked from the NDE SEL page as 'Nevada Social Emotional Standards'). Page 1 defines the five competencies; page 2 lists the 15 standards in a two-column layout. Grouping (1-3 Self-Awareness, 4-6 Self-Management, 7-9 Social Awareness, 10-12 Relationship Skills, 13-15 Responsible Decision Making) was confirmed from text-block positions on the page, because plain text extraction scrambles the column order. The PDF gives only short titles, so the summaries are brief paraphrases built from those titles and the document's glossary (self-efficacy, growth mindset, agency are marked with an asterisk there). The 'K-12' grade label comes from NDE's pre-K page, not from this PDF. Adoption year left blank: the file date (April 2025) is not a stated adoption date.

items.title: Develop personal interests and self-efficacy
items.summary: Build personal interests and confidence in one's ability to reach goals (the state defines self-efficacy that way).

items.title: Identify emotions
items.summary: Recognize and name one's own emotions.

items.title: Cultivate a growth mindset
items.summary: Believe abilities can improve through practice, taking on challenges and learning from mistakes (the state's glossary meaning of growth mindset).

items.title: Regulate emotions
items.summary: Respond to and manage emotions and thoughts in different situations.

items.title: Set and achieve goals
items.summary: Set goals and work toward them, personally and collectively.

items.title: Develop agency
items.summary: Build the freedom and ownership to make choices and take intentional action (the state's glossary meaning of agency).

items.title: Recognize the emotions and perspectives of others
items.summary: Notice and understand how other people feel and see things.

items.title: Demonstrate empathy and compassion
items.summary: Show empathy and compassion toward others.

items.title: Communicate effectively
items.summary: Communicate clearly and listen actively with others.

items.title: Practice teamwork and collaborative problem-solving
items.summary: Work together with others to solve problems.

items.title: Seek and offer support when needed
items.summary: Ask for help and give help to others when it is needed.

items.title: Cultivate curiosity and open-mindedness
items.summary: Stay curious and open to other ideas and viewpoints.

items.title: Make reasoned decisions and judgments
items.summary: Make careful, well-reasoned choices and judgments.

items.title: Understand the impact of one's actions
items.summary: Consider how one's own actions affect oneself and others.

frameworks.name: Portrait of a Nevada Learner
frameworks.issuingBody: Nevada Department of Education (with the Nevada Future of Learning Network)
frameworks.notes: Read from the 2-page 'Portrait of a Nevada Learner' pamphlet (PDF dated December 2023) linked from the NDE page: https://www.nvfutureoflearning.org/_files/ugd/edc730_4d8bc57c3d84481d8e26d50b8a72b3f0.pdf. Four attributes (Empowering, Connecting, Impacting, Thriving), each with a guiding question and 3-4 'I' statements; the items below summarise each attribute. Caveats: the PDF is hosted on the Future of Learning Network site (nvfutureoflearning.org), not doe.nv.gov, although NDE links to it and describes it as the guiding vision and 'key outcomes for each learner'. The document is called a Portrait of a Learner, not Graduate. Adoption year not stated; the 2021-22 co-design date comes from the NDE page. No State Board adoption found.

items.title: Empowering: How will I grow in my learning?
items.summary: Know one's strengths, stay curious with a growth attitude, be self-aware and advocate for oneself, and ask for support to keep a balance across intellectual, physical, mental, social and emotional well-being.

items.title: Connecting: How do I build and sustain relationships and community?
items.summary: Listen actively and collaborate, adapt communication to different audiences and tools, and show empathy and respect for people of different backgrounds and viewpoints.

items.title: Impacting: How will I contribute to make an impact?
items.summary: Apply knowledge across subjects for a purpose, think critically and creatively to solve problems, and take part in community and civic life.

items.title: Thriving: How will I thrive?
items.summary: Stay resilient and courageous through change and mistakes, keep learning, unlearning and relearning, and act with integrity by keeping commitments and staying true to one's values.

alignments.rationale: FNE lesson "Trust Your Growth" (series: Confidence & Courage; the objective is the same in every grade version). FNE's stated objective: "Students will understand that growth does not always happen quickly or dramatically. They will learn to recognize progress, avoid comparison, respect small steps, and build confidence by trusting what is being developed inside them."
